name: json-rust (json crate, DOM parser)
baseline: serde_json 1.0.72, both serde_json::Value (DOM) and typed struct parsing
verdict_reason: The README says it can even outperform parsing to structs, but in the benchmark it links (2021 run) json-rust DOM parsing at 390-520 MB/s was slower than serde_json struct parsing at 550-710 MB/s on all three files. Its lead over serde_json's Value was real but is five years old, and the crate has had no release since 2020, carries an unmaintained advisory with an open soundness report, and was dropped from that benchmark in 2023.
tier_reason: Public benchmark code (serde-rs/json-benchmark) with the CPU and rustc nightly stated; it is maintained by serde_json's author.
claimed_speedup: DOM parse 390 vs 320 MB/s (canada), 520 vs 420 MB/s (citm_catalog), 430 vs 300 MB/s (twitter) against serde_json's Value; DOM stringify 840 vs 430, 780 vs 560, 1030 vs 910 MB/s. serde_json struct parse in the same run: 580, 710 and 550 MB/s.
workload: nativejson-benchmark files canada.json, citm_catalog.json, twitter.json; DOM parse and stringify; best of two runs.
one_liner: Untyped JSON DOM crate that beat serde_json's Value in a 2021 run but not serde_json struct parsing; unmaintained since 2020.
how_it_is_fast: Parses only to its own dynamic JsonValue, with no serde layer, and stores numbers as a 64-bit mantissa plus 16-bit decimal exponent instead of converting to f64 during parsing.
use_it_when: Do not adopt it for new code; serde_json, simd-json or sonic-rs cover the same DOM use
skip_it_when: Any new project: no release since 0.12.4 (2020-03-18) and RUSTSEC-2022-0081 flags it unmaintained
Typed parsing: it has no struct deserialization
caveats: Numbers are from a December 2021 run with serde_json 1.0.72; serde_json has changed a lot since
The benchmark is maintained by serde_json's author
json-rust was removed from the suite in 2023 citing the open soundness issue
tradeoffs: Unmaintained with a possible soundness issue (json-rust issue 196)
Its number representation differs from f64 semantics used by most JSON crates

evidence.quote: It does [very well in benchmarks](https://github.com/serde-rs/json-benchmark), in some cases it can even outperform parsing to structs.
